layers.note: A summer annual grass of open ground between shrubs, after the monsoon.

moisture.note: Mesas, deserts and foothills in open ground (Hitchcock).

elevation_m.note: Up to 5,500 feet in Arizona (Kearney and Peebles).

shade_tolerance.note: Open ground; light shade under shrubs.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 5 to 18 °C; gone below 2 °C and above 22 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −10 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −14 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 27 to 34 °C; gone below 24 °C, where summers are too short, and above 37 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 5,500 to 11,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 4,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 3,800 to 9,200 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 3,000.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.05 to 0.4, gone by 0.02 and above 0.5.

summer_rain.note: Needs the monsoon's summer rain: from about 0.4 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone below 0.3; up to about 0.85, gone by 0.95.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Needle grama grows from Texas to southern California and northern Mexico, and in Argentina (Hitchcock; Kearney and Peebles). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
